title: Owners, operators and managers
description: The companies at the economic and operational layers — the ones that can sign a contract. Container lines are here because they are named, ranked and reachable; the bulk and tanker owners whose ships are actually being sunk are harder to enumerate and are the main gap in this library.

records.name: MSC Mediterranean Shipping Company
records.ownership: Private. Wholly owned by the Aponte-Diamant family; founded 1970 by Gianluigi Aponte and Rafaela Aponte-Diamant.

key_people.name: Soren Toft
key_people.note: First CEO from outside the family, from December 2020

records.market_share_note: 21.2% of global container capacity as of November 2025 per a separate count; passed 7 million TEU in November 2025.

records.name: CMA CGM
records.note: CMA CGM Symi was targeted on 24 November 2023, five days into the campaign.

records.name: COSCO Shipping
records.note: State-owned. Transited the Red Sea through periods when Western carriers would not. Not a prospect; a benchmark for what the risk is worth to someone with a different threat profile.

records.name: Ocean Network Express
records.ownership: Joint venture of NYK, MOL and K Line

records.name: Cosmoship Management S.A.
records.fleet_note: Manager of the Eternity C, sunk 7-8 July 2025 with loss of life and five months of crew captivity.

records.name: Third-party technical managers
records.note: Named from general industry knowledge, not from a source in this register. Verify fleet counts against Equasis DOC records before use.

gaps: No tanker owners: Frontline, Tsakos, Euronav/CMB.TECH, Angelicoussis. Tankers are the segment being hit.
No dry bulk owners beyond Cosmoship. Bulk carriers were 62% of Malacca and Singapore incidents in H1 2026 and account for most named Red Sea losses.
No charterers at all: the oil majors and traders — Shell, BP, Vitol, Trafigura, Cargill — who bear the war-risk premium under most charter parties.
No P&I clubs or war-risk brokers, who influence the purchase without making it.
Container market-share figures come from an aggregator. Replace with Alphaliner or Linerlytica before quoting externally.
